summary: Rowan County's history says a 48-foot wooden lookout tower stood on Young's Mountain from 1954 until its removal in June 1968.

facts.status_note: Tower removed in June 1968 per the Rowan County history; no source describes what remains on the summit.

events.note: Young's Mountain Tower removed in June 1968

evidence.supports: summit located in Rowan County, NC
evidence.quote: Youngs Mountain is a summit located in Rowan County, NC
at an elevation of 1089 ft MSL.

evidence.supports: Rowan County entered a cooperative agreement with the state in 1949
evidence.quote: In 1949, Rowan County entered into a cooperative agreement with the state.

evidence.supports: 48-foot wooden tower built on Young's Mountain in September 1954
evidence.quote: In September 1954, a 48-foot wooden tower was built on Young's Mountain.

evidence.supports: 73-foot High Rock tower built in 1955 at Healing Springs, Davidson County
evidence.quote: In 1955, the 73-foot High Rock Lookout Tower was built at Healing Springs in Davidson County.

evidence.quote: located on the north side of Lake Lure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Rowan County history spells it Young's Mountain; TopoQuest uses Youngs Mountain. The tnlandforms record and this brief use Youngs Mountain.

notes_for_editor: Built and removal dates rest on one county government history page (not a register). No photo, staffing, cab or height-to-cab-floor data found, so the height is not recorded. Record status was unknown; facts.status 'removed' comes from that page. The Conserving Carolina trail is a different Youngs Mountain near Lake Lure and is flagged in the story. Not checked: NC Forest Service records, Rowan Public Library holdings, NHLR/FFLOS (no cached entry), and any site visit or current condition. The NGS mark FA 5349 in the record was not verified.
